body:
I can verify that curve tilt is interpolated linearly, causing these abrupt changes. I would expect the result to be a cubic interpolation, given that the interpolation in bezier curves is also cubic. Would there need to be a similar "in/out" strength for tilt interpolation, in the same way as the curve points, or would that be unnecessary?
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01f995fa-6234-4926-85b1-9b9542779f48)

Digging into the code a bit, it seems that the issue might be with the baking. It looks like the basis is being slerped between baked points, so that should produce the correct results. Actually, I just confirmed it's an issue with the baking, as I set the bake interval to a large value so it will interpolate along the whole spline, and the orange curve ended up being straight and red was curved, as is the expected behavior. So the baked cache of the tilt (or the spacing of them) is what's broken. I think the problem is here: ```c++ bfw[pidx] = _calculate_tangent(points[i].position, points[i].position + points[i].out, points[i + 1].position + points[i + 1].in, points[i + 1].position, E.key); btw[pidx] = Math::lerp(points[i].tilt, points[i + 1].tilt, E.key); ``` _calculate_tangent is doing a `bezier_derivative()`, however the tilt is just using a simple lerp on E.key (E is the midpoints), which does not reflect the accurate distance of the curve.
